---
title: "Cox regression"
subtitle: "Survival analysis across three hospitals"
---

```{python}
#| echo: false
import os
os.environ.setdefault("OMP_NUM_THREADS", "2")
```

The DLBCL cohort of Rosenwald et al. (2002), split by molecular
subgroup. GCB, ABC and Type III lymphomas arise from different cells
of origin and tend to be diagnosed at different referral centers, so
using the subgroup as the site boundary is operationally realistic
rather than a convenience — and it produces genuinely imbalanced
sites.

Each site computes its own Cox partial log-likelihood at the current
coefficient vector. Patient rows never leave.

```{python}
from homomorphepy.examples import cox

fit = cox.run(backend="threshold")
```

```{python}
#| echo: false
from IPython.display import Markdown

sizes = " · ".join(f"{k} n={v} ({fit.site_events[k]} events)"
                   for k, v in fit.site_sizes.items())
rows = "\n".join(
    f"| `{r['coefficient']}` | {r['distributed_encrypted']:.6f} "
    f"| {r['aggregated_cleartext']:.6f} | {r['abs_diff']:.1e} |"
    for r in fit.table()
)
Markdown(
    f"Sites: {sizes}\n\n"
    "| coefficient | distributed, encrypted | centralized cleartext | difference |\n"
    "|---|---|---|---|\n" + rows
)
```

The distributed encrypted fit and the centralized fit agree to
`{python} f"{fit.max_abs_difference:.1e}"`, over
`{python} fit.n_objective_calls` objective evaluations — each one a
full encrypt, homomorphic sum, and n-of-n threshold decryption across
the three sites.

Log-likelihood: `{python} f"{fit.loglik_encrypted:.6f}"` encrypted
against `{python} f"{fit.loglik_centralized:.6f}"` centralized.

## Only the master class changes

The single-decrypter and threshold versions differ in one line. The
optimizer, the objective, the site functions and the protocol runner
are identical; swapping the backend swaps who can decrypt.

```{python}
ckks_fit = cox.run(backend="ckks")
```

```{python}
#| echo: false
Markdown(f"""
| backend | max diff vs centralized | can any single party decrypt? |
|---|---|---|
| single-decrypter CKKS | {ckks_fit.max_abs_difference:.1e} | yes, the master |
| threshold (n-of-n) | {fit.max_abs_difference:.1e} | no |
""")
```

## Two tie conventions, on purpose

`survival::coxph` defaults to Efron's method for tied event times;
`statsmodels` defaults to Breslow's. On this cohort, where follow-up
is recorded to a tenth of a year across 235 patients, the two differ
by up to 3.56 in pooled log-likelihood — a silent wrong answer, not an
error, if the argument is forgotten.

This example passes `ties="efron"` to match R. The
[Cox-lasso](cox-lasso.qmd) example uses Breslow instead, because its
partial likelihood is written symbolically for a convex solver and
that form *is* Breslow's; Efron has no comparable formulation. The R
vignettes make exactly the same split.
